doc.title: Jillean Williams interviewed by Milt Fillius and Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 20, 1995

title: Student drummer Paul Wells sits in for a week with Joe
summary: A William Paterson student drummer, booked by Norman Simmons, learned Joe's music quickly and impressed audiences.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: We had a, I don’t know if Joe told you this, but he was working in Washington, DC last week and they didn’t have a drummer. Norman, who, Norman Simmons booked a drummer who is a student at William Paterson College. Did they tell you this? And his name is Paul Wells. And Norman thought he showed great promise and so he booked him for this job. And Paul had to take finals during the week of the gig. So he said I can’t miss this opportunity, so he went to his principal and said, “I have a chance to work for a week with Joe Williams, and could I postpone taking my finals for a while?” They said, “go, go, this is the best experience you’ll ever have.” So we had him for a week.

He was terrific. He was a charming young man, 21 years old, very interested, keen, watched Norman like a hawk because he didn’t know Joe’s music at all. We never met him until the first show, like five minutes before the first show, and Joe had trouble with his name, because it was unfamiliar. Anyway, he really worked hard. He listened to Joe, he listened to Henry Johnson, the guitar player who was helping him, and he just was fantastic. I mean “Roll ‘Em Pete” when he has all those exchanges with Joe, he was fabulous. People were applauding in the middle of the song. So there’s one that shows promise. But like you say, what does he do when he graduates?
Yeah. What does he do for an encore?
Well maybe he’ll go with Joe Williams on the road. But he had a wonderful time and he was awfully good, and that was very encouraging.
